paper.title: Practical and Optimal Algorithm for Linear Contextual Bandits with Rare Parameter Updates

settings.name_in_paper: Linear Contextual Bandits with Batched Feedback (rare parameter updates)
unmapped: Context sets of K arms drawn i.i.d. from an unknown distribution D each round (arbitrary correlation within a round)
Parameter estimate updated only at O(log log T) static-grid times; reward-free within-interval adaptivity allowed
settings.definition_quote: At each round $t \in [T]$, the agent observes contextual features of $K$ arms $\mathcal{A}_t := \{x_{t,1}, \dots, x_{t,K}\} \subseteq \RR^d$ and selects one arm $x_{t,a_t} \in \mathcal{A}_t$, receiving the reward $r_t = \langle x_{t,a_t}, \theta^* \rangle + \eta_t$ ... we assume that each feature set $\mathcal{A}_t$ is drawn i.i.d. from an unknown distribution $\mathcal{D}$ across rounds

settings.name_in_paper: Generalized Linear Contextual Bandits with Batched Feedback
unmapped: Rewards almost surely in [0,R] with R known to the learner (implies self-concordance |mu''| <= R mu')
Context sets drawn i.i.d. from unknown distribution D
Rare parameter updates (O(log log T) static grid)
settings.definition_quote: We next consider generalized linear contextual bandits, where rewards follow a one-parameter exponential family distribution... Following sawarni2024generalized, we assume i.i.d. contexts drawn from an unknown distribution $\mathcal D$ and rewards almost surely supported on $[0,R]$ for a known constant $R>0$.

conditions: context sets i.i.d. from unknown D

source.label: thm:BLCE_g
source.quote: Suppose that Assumptions~\ref{assum:norm} and \ref{assum:subgauss} hold and that the context sets $\{\mathcal{A}_t\}_{t=1}^T$ are drawn i.i.d. from an unknown distribution $\mathcal{D}$. Run BLCE-G for $T$ rounds, using $\lambda = \log (dT)$, and any fixed constant $c\in(0,1)$. The worst-case cumulative regret satisfies $\mathcal{R}(T) = \Ocal(\sqrt{dT}(\sqrt{\log(KT)} \wedge \sqrt{d+\log T})\sqrt{\log d\log\log T}) = \tilde{\Ocal}(\sqrt{dT\log K} \wedge d\sqrt{T})$.

results.notes: Also stated as O_tilde(sqrt(dT log K) ∧ d sqrt(T)). Uses O(log log T) parameter updates. Regret defined via means, so pseudo-regret. Proof uses d>=3 in a step.

conditions: context sets i.i.d. from unknown D (relaxable to batch-wise conditions of Remark 1)

source.label: thm:BLCE
source.quote: Suppose that Assumptions~\ref{assum:norm} and \ref{assum:subgauss} hold and that the context sets $\{A_t\}_{t=1}^T$ are drawn i.i.d. from an unknown distribution $\mathcal{D}$. Run BLCE for $T$ rounds, using $\lambda = 1$, and any fixed constant $c\in(0,1)$. The worst-case cumulative regret satisfies $\mathcal{R}(T) = \Ocal(\sqrt{dT}(\sqrt{\log(KT)} \wedge \sqrt{d+\log T})\sqrt{\log T\log\log T}) = \tilde{\Ocal}(\sqrt{dT\log K} \wedge d\sqrt{T})$.

results.notes: Also O_tilde(sqrt(dT log K) ∧ d sqrt T). Remark 1 says guarantee holds under weaker batch-wise conditional independence conditions. Time complexity O(K d^2 T log log T).

bound.expression_latex: \Ocal \Big(RS\sqrt{d(d+\log T)T\log T\log\log T / \hat\kappa}\Big) + \Ocal \bigg(\Big(R^2Se^{8RS}d(d+\log T)\log T\log\log T + \frac{R}{\log\log T} \Big)T^{\frac{1}{3}} \bigg)

symbols.R_r: known bound on the reward support [0,R]
symbols.kappa_hat: 1 / E_{A~D}[mu'(<x*,theta*>)], reciprocal of average curvature at the optimal arm

conditions: log-partition m convex and three times differentiable
context sets i.i.d. from unknown D

source.label: thm:bgle
source.quote: Suppose that Assumptions~\ref{assum:GLM_norm} and \ref{assum:GLM_diff} hold, that the context sets are drawn i.i.d. from an unknown distribution $\mathcal{D}$, and that rewards are almost surely supported on $[0,R]$. ... Run BGLE for $T$ rounds, using the known bounds $R$ and $S$, $\lambda=R^2(d+\log T)$, and any fixed constant $c\in(0,1)$ ... The worst-case cumulative regret satisfies $\mathcal{R}(T) = \Ocal (RS\sqrt{d(d+\log T)T\log T\log\log T / \hat\kappa}) + \Ocal ((R^2Se^{8RS}d(d+\log T)\log T\log\log T + \frac{R}{\log\log T})T^{1/3})$

results.notes: Paper calls it worst-case but bound depends on instance quantity kappa_hat; marked instance_dependent. Also stated as O_tilde(RSd sqrt(T)/sqrt(kappa_hat)) + O_tilde((R^2 S e^{8RS} d^2 + R) T^{1/3}).
